extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: Visual Genome is a dataset for connecting language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations. It contains over 100K images with dense annotations of objects, attributes, relationships, region descriptions, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The first release uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO. Workers drew bounding boxes and wrote region descriptions, extracted objects from descriptions and grounded them with boxes, added attributes and relationships to form region graphs, merged region graphs into scene graphs, and wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs. Data were collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some descriptions like "it is a sunny day" do not contain any objects and therefore have no region graphs associated with them. Workers are asked to not generate any graphs for such descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The first release of the Visual Genome dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Scene graphs are created by combining all region graphs for an image and merging nodes that correspond to the same object. Objects from different graphs are considered the same if their bounding boxes have an overlap over union of 0.8, and workers confirm such merges. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools, WordNet lexeme counts, hand-crafted mapping rules, and worker verification.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To collect diverse region descriptions, BLEU score thresholds of 0.7 were enforced against previously written image-specific descriptions and the top 100 most common global descriptions. Bounding boxes were required to satisfy coverage and quality constraints. Stanford dependency parsing was used to suggest nouns for object extraction. For canonicalization, Stanford NLP tools extracted noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs; attributes were normalized by morphology; relationships were mapped using WordNet sentence frames and root hypernyms; mappings were then verified by workers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers. For each new image, workers drew three bounding boxes and wrote three region descriptions; this was repeated until 50 region descriptions were collected per image. Workers then extracted objects from each description and grounded them with bounding boxes, added attributes to objects and relationships between object pairs to form region graphs, and wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs. Verification used majority voting for all components except objects, and rapid judgments for object verification. Canonicalization mappings to WordNet were also verified by workers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using majority voting and rapid judgments. All components except objects were verified by three unique workers voting on factual correctness, and an annotation was added if at least two of three workers verified it. Objects were verified using rapid judgments. For canonicalization, workers were shown the proposed synset and four alternatives without being told which was the proposed one, and asked to select the best fit. The paper also reports precision and recall for canonicalization: objects 88.0 precision and 98.5 recall, attributes 85.7 precision and 95.9 recall, relationships 92.9 precision and 88.5 recall.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Region descriptions: 50 per image; freeform QA: 8 per image task; each annotation verification used 3 workers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. 93.02% were from the United States, 1.29% from the Philippines, 1.13% from Kenya, 0.94% from India, 0.50% from Russia, 0.47% from Canada, and 2.65% from other countries. The majority of workers were between 25 and 34 years old. The gender split was 54.15% male and 45.85% female. The youngest contributor was 18 years old and the oldest was 68 years old.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser, Stanford NLP tools (CoreNLP), BLEU score computation, WordNet
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper refers to the first release of the Visual Genome dataset and notes that the crowdsourcing strategies were deployed in the ongoing effort of collecting the dataset. Further visualizations, API, and additional information can be found online. No explicit versioning timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator demographics including geographic location, age, and gender were collected and reported.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable training and benchmarking of the next generation of computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, including applications such as image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. Certain sports such as skiing and surfing are overrepresented due to a bias in the image set. The paper also notes that common visual concepts like colors and frequent phrases can dominate descriptions without diversity controls.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. Some descriptions contain no explicit objects and therefore have no region graphs. The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, and certain sports are overrepresented. The paper also notes that current models trained on the dataset still struggle with complex reasoning and detailed image understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding. Explicit use cases discussed include object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, semantic image retrieval, relationship extraction, and image understanding evaluation.
